notes: sig uses DSL type syntax and may be a list of overloads (the first overload whose parameter types accept the arguments wins); <T>/<U> are generic parameters. method: true => callable as receiver.name(args) (receiver = first param); a direct call name(receiver, …) is also legal. property: true => accessed as receiver.name without parentheses (lowered to ["f", name, [receiver]]).
Optional receivers: x.m(…) and x.p with x: T? are null-propagating — the result is null when x is null and the result type becomes U?. A direct call m(x) requires a non-optional x.
Overloads, not unions: contains/isEmpty have a string overload and a list overload; anything else is a type error.
Lambdas are legal only as arguments of stdlib functions. Lambdas passed to map/filter/find/some/every may declare 1 or 2 parameters: (item) or (item, index).

Rounding everywhere = half away from zero. Reference: t = trunc(x); |x − t| >= 0.5 ? t + sign(x) : t (Kotlin: do not use kotlin.math.round (half-even) or Math.round (half-up)). round(0.49999999999999994) = 0.

Fixed-point formatting (str and formatNumber), with d fraction digits: if |x| >= 1e15 — digits = exact integer digits of round-half-away(x) (for formatNumber followed by d zeros). Otherwise scaled = |x| * 10^d computed in double; r = round-half-away(scaled); digits = exact decimal expansion of r as an integer (Swift: String(format: "%.0f", r); Kotlin: BigDecimal(r).toPlainString()), with the point inserted d digits from the right (left-padding with zeros). Sign: prefix '-' iff x < 0 and at least one printed digit is non-zero. Never round a decimal string representation: formatNumber(2.675, 2) = '2.68' (2.675*100 == 267.5 in binary64), formatNumber(1.005, 2) = '1.00' (1.005*100 == 100.49999999999999).

Number to string (str, interpolation, join): integral and |n| < 1e15 => integer digits without fraction; |n| >= 1e15 => exact integer digits of round-half-away(n); otherwise the fixed-point rule with d = 6, then trailing zeros (and a trailing '.') trimmed. -0 prints '0'. NaN => 'NaN', +/-Infinity => 'Infinity'/'-Infinity'. Decimal separator is always '.'.

str(string) is the identity. str of list/record => compact JSON: record keys sorted by code point; strings escape only '"', '\\' and U+0000–U+001F (\n \r \t \b \f, others \u00xx); '/' and non-ASCII are raw; nested numbers use the number rule above; str(null) => 'null'; bool => 'true'/'false'; token values => their JSON encoding.

Strings are sequences of Unicode code points (scalars): length, indices, substring, comparison (<, sortBy) and equality operate on code points, with no normalization ('e\u0301' != '\u00e9'; U+FF01 < U+1F600). Swift must not use String.count/==/<; Kotlin must not use UTF-16 length/compareTo/substring.
Arithmetic is IEEE-754 double: x/0 => ±Infinity or NaN, % is fmod (sign of the dividend).

Equality (==) is deep and structural: numbers by value (NaN != NaN), strings by code points, lists elementwise, records by key set + values (order-insensitive), token values by encoding. == and != accept T against T?.
All values are immutable. Assignment replaces the state value with an updated copy; locals never alias state (let before = items; items[0].done = true leaves before unchanged).

Indices: xs[i] (lists) is null unless i is an integer with 0 <= i < count; m[k] (map<T>, k: string) is null for a missing key — both lower to ["at", obj, key]. set/removeAt with such an index return an unchanged copy. Path assignment with an invalid index, or through a null/missing intermediate, is a no-op. substring/slice floor fractional arguments, NaN counts as 0.

Runtime token values: color => {"$color": name} (+"alpha": a when alpha() applied), gradient => {"$gradient": [colors], "angle": deg}, textStyle => {"$type": name}, motion => {"$motion": name} or {"$motion": {spec}}, icon => {"$icon": name}. @space.* and @radius.* evaluate to numbers from the active theme.

round.doc: half away from zero: round(2.5)=3, round(-2.5)=-3

clamp.sig: (x: number, lo: number, hi: number) => number

interpolate.sig: (x: number, input: list<number>, output: list<number>) => number
interpolate.doc: piecewise linear over input stops, clamped to the first/last output outside the range. Input stops must be non-decreasing and lengths equal with at least 2 stops, else output.first ?? 0. At a duplicated stop the later segment applies.

upper.doc: full case mapping applied per code point, locale-independent, without context rules (no final-sigma rule)

lower.doc: full case mapping applied per code point, locale-independent, without context rules (no final-sigma rule)

trim.doc: strips leading/trailing White_Space code points: U+0009–000D, 0020, 0085, 00A0, 1680, 2000–200A, 2028, 2029, 202F, 205F, 3000

contains.doc: overloads: (string, string) substring test ('' => true); (list<T>, T) deep-equality membership

split.doc: keeps empty parts: 'a,,b'.split(',') = ['a','','b']; empty sep => list of single code points

replace.sig: (s: string, a: string, b: string) => string
replace.doc: all literal occurrences; empty a => s unchanged

matches.doc: whole-string match. \d \w \s are Unicode-aware on both platforms (Kotlin compiles with Pattern.UNICODE_CHARACTER_CLASS). Use only the common subset: classes [], \d \w \s, quantifiers * + ? {m,n}, groups, alternation, anchors

substring.sig: (s: string, start: number, end?: number) => string
substring.doc: code point indices, clamped to [0, length]; end defaults to length; start >= end => ''

num.doc: after trim must match ^[+-]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][+-]?\d+)?$ and be finite, else null (no NaN/Infinity/hex/suffixes)

map.sig: <T, U>(xs: list<T>, f: (T, number) => U) => list<U>

reduce.sig: <T, U>(xs: list<T>, init: U, f: (U, T) => U) => U

set.sig: <T>(xs: list<T>, i: number, v: T) => list<T>

slice.sig: <T>(xs: list<T>, start: number, end?: number) => list<T>

sortBy.doc: keys must be all number or all string (compile-time); stable ascending; numbers numerically with NaN after all numbers, strings by code points

range.doc: [0, 1, …, floor(n)-1]; n <= 0 or non-finite => []; n capped at 10000

with.doc: patch must be a record literal whose fields are a subset of r's fields, each assignable; r must be a non-optional record (or null-propagating per notes). Result type R.

formatNumber.doc: decimals = clamp(floor(d), 0, 10); fixed-point rule from notes; the integer digits of the rounded result are grouped by 3 from the right with U+00A0: formatNumber(1990, 0) = '1 990', formatNumber(999.999, 2) = '1 000.00'; non-finite x prints like str

formatDuration.doc: negative or non-finite => 0; whole seconds (floor). hms => 'HH:MM:SS' (hours unbounded, >=2 digits); ms => 'MM:SS' (minutes unbounded, >=2 digits); dhms => 'D:HH:MM:SS' (days without padding)

formatDate.doc: epoch ms in env.timeZone (unknown zone => UTC): date => 'dd.MM.yyyy', time => 'HH:mm', dateTime => 'dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm'; non-finite => ''

plural.sig: (n: number, forms: {one?: string, few?: string, many?: string, other: string}) => string
plural.doc: language = lowercase of env.locale up to the first '-' or '_'. 'ru': i=|trunc(n)|, integer n only: i%10==1 && i%100!=11 => one; i%10 in 2..4 && i%100 not in 12..14 => few; else many; non-integer n => other. 'en','az','ka','uz','ab','kk': |n| == 1 => one else other. Any other language => other. Missing form => other; 'other' is required (compile-time). Every '#' in the chosen form is replaced by str(n).

gradient.doc: CSS semantics: 0 = to top, 90 = to right

alpha.doc: a clamped to [0,1] and multiplied into any existing alpha; the alpha key is omitted when the product is 1, so alpha(c, 1) == c

curve.sig: (duration: number, x1: number, y1: number, x2: number, y2: number) => motion

open.doc: https or a host-allowlisted scheme; anything else is ignored

refresh.doc: argument is a bare data-source name, lowered to ["v", name]

play.doc: bare timeline name; restarts from 0; `await play(x)` resumes when every instance finished (never for repeat -1)

stop.doc: removes the timeline's effect (values return to identity)

callResult: {ok: bool, value: <op result>?, error: {code: string, message: string}?, fieldErrors: map<string>?}

language.escapes: string escapes: \" \\ \n \t \$ (literal '$', so "\${x}" is the 4-char text ${x}) \u{HEX}; any other escape is a compile error
language.coalesce: ?? is right-associative; null is assignable to every T?; a: T?, b: T => T; b: T? => T?
language.event: event is a contextual keyword: a declaration at template top level (`event tap`); inside on.* bodies an expression of the event payload type; anywhere else a compile error; on the wire the payload is the local ["l", "event"]
language.declarations: state initializers see params, data, env, earlier state, fns and tokens; let and fn are order-independent (cycles/recursion are errors); fn bodies see only their parameters, other fns, stdlib, env and tokens
language.data: data without `required` has type R?, with `required` R; args may reference only literals and params
language.effects: refresh/play/stop take a bare name, lowered to ["v", name]; await is legal before call and play only
language.bind: `bind` is a pseudo-prop inside textField props: bind: "x" == value: =x plus on.change: x = event.value
language.repeat: repeat.over accepts list<T> or list<T>? (null renders nothing)
language.types: map<T> is string-keyed; a record-typed value is assignable to map<T> when every field is assignable to T; a field k?: T may be omitted and reads as T?; unions (incl. mixed like number | "fill") may be written in annotations; `any` exists only in contract signatures; a record literal assigned to a record type may not contain fields absent from that type (compile error naming the field)
language.timelines: equal key times act as a step to the later key; duplicate (target, prop) tracks in one timeline are a compile error; repeat must be >= 1 or -1
